new_entities.name: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist therapy for HFrEF
aliases: spironolactone or eplerenone in reduced-EF heart failure
MRA treatment in systolic heart failure
new_entities.description: Use of spironolactone-class mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.

edges.effect_quant: RALES reduced death with spironolactone (RR 0.70), EMPHASIS-HF reduced all-cause death with eplerenone (HR 0.76), and pooled individual-patient data from RALES, EMPHASIS-HF, and TOPCAT showed sustained mortality and morbidity benefit.
edges.population: adults with chronic HFrEF across severe and mild symptomatic spectra receiving standard heart-failure therapy
edges.mechanism: Mineralocorticoid receptor blockade counteracts maladaptive aldosterone signaling, reducing myocardial fibrosis, arrhythmic vulnerability, sodium retention, and progressive ventricular remodeling.
edges.summary: MRA therapy is a core mortality-reducing pillar in HFrEF. The signal is strong across classic severe-HF and milder-symptom trial populations, with hyperkalemia and renal monitoring as the main tradeoff.
edges.caveats: The benefit is clearest when patients can safely tolerate potassium and renal-function monitoring. The factor slug names spironolactone, but the evidence base here includes the class signal from both spironolactone and eplerenone.

evidence.citation: Pitt B et al 1999 N Engl J Med
evidence.notes: The effect of spironolactone on morbidity and mortality in patients with severe heart failure. Randomized Aldactone Evaluation Study Investigators.

effect_quant.comparator: all-cause mortality in RALES with spironolactone versus placebo

evidence.citation: Zannad F et al 2011 N Engl J Med
evidence.notes: Eplerenone in patients with systolic heart failure and mild symptoms.

effect_quant.comparator: all-cause mortality in EMPHASIS-HF with eplerenone versus placebo

evidence.citation: Ferreira JP et al 2019 JACC Heart Fail
evidence.notes: MRAs in Elderly HF Patients: Individual Patient-Data Meta-Analysis of RALES, EMPHASIS-HF, and TOPCAT.
